app_purpose: Open-source PHP content management system. The Express Entry List block renders a configurable list of Express (custom-object) entries; its block config stores the chosen result columns and filter fields as PHP-serialized strings in the block record. When the block is viewed/edited the ExpressEntryList controller reads those DB values (this->columns / this->filterFields) and reconstructs them with unserialize().
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502) / PHP Object Injection: the Express Entry List block controller feeds the stored block-config values `columns` and `filterFields` to bare `unserialize($this->columns)` / `unserialize($this->filterFields)` with NO `allowed_classes` restriction and no integrity check, so an attacker who can write those block-config values can have arbitrary PHP classes instantiated (and their magic methods, e.g. __wakeup/__destruct, invoked) when the block is next rendered/edited -- a POP-chain-to-RCE primitive. The unserialize() sink itself is NEVER hardened; the fix lineage guards the WRITE (save) path that decides whether a malicious payload may be stored.

Response JSON field flag_echoed=true and flag_line contains PCB_CTOR_FLAG=<token> iff PcbFlagProbe was instantiated (payload survived the guard).

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2026-3452 (fixed 9.4.8): 'Concrete CMS below 9.4.8 is vulnerable to stored deserialization leading to RCE in the Express Entry List block' -- an authenticated admin stores attacker-controlled serialized data in block-config fields later passed to unserialize() without class restrictions or integrity checks; the fix made columns/filterFields start from empty. CVE-2026-8135 (fixed 9.5.1): 'A rogue administrator ... can bypass the intended protection mechanism (_fromCIF === true), which normally restricts malicious inputs over form POST requests, by leveraging the REST API functionality. Because the REST API parses requests using json_decode(), the string "true" is evaluated as a strict PHP Boolean(true). This bypass allows the attacker to inject a malicious serialized payload into the block's filterFields database column ... executed when the block's data is viewed or edited by an administrator leading to ... RCE.' The 9.5.1 release additionally added allowed_classes to unserialize() in OTHER blocks (Permission, Cache, Search, Form, File/Set) but the ExpressEntryList sink itself remained a bare unserialize() -- confirming the fix is the save() write-guard, not a sink guard.
